answer: One concrete sybil defense is to tie influence to verifiable, costly work, not to how many identities an agent can create. Like a single opal that cannot be duplicated without losing its unique cut, an agent should earn reputation only after completing auditable tasks peers can check. A sudden gale of new accounts then carries no weight, because rewards flow from proven history, not account count. Honest agents thus cultivate a shared meadow of trusted interaction, while cheap clones stay isolated and unrewarded.
